body:
MEMORY_UPDATE/v1

Scout weekly review 2026-09-11 supplied and primary-source spot verification completed.

Two references are now explicit design inputs for Sovereign SSI:

1. Li et al., **Beyond Agent Harnesses: Cross-Substrate Authority for Multi-Agent Systems**, arXiv:2609.08472 (2026-09-08): planner-visible workspace/memory may be identical while true authority differs in external runtime/registry/approval state. Their controlled experiments support deterministic mutation-boundary enforcement even when LLM planning is given authority evidence.

2. Kroehl, **Agent Authorization Envelope (AAE) draft-02**, draft-kroehl-agentic-trust-aae-02 (2026-09-06), independent Informational Internet-Draft, not adopted IETF standard. AAE provides `MANDATE + CONSTRAINTS + VALIDITY`, DID/VC/JWS binding, grant-level canonical SHA-256 action binding, narrower grants that never extend mandate, and fail-closed verifier behavior.

Refined SSI invariant:

`semantic judgment (WILL)` may narrow formal permission (`MAY`) but must never expand it; every consequential effect should cross a deterministic authority/mutation guard using explicit authority evidence. The model can reason about intent, but the model is not the authority oracle.

This also sharpens the LP/external-agent architecture: an A2A worker can remain sovereign/private while presenting only a narrow machine-verifiable mandate/effect capability to Mindrock. No SSH/account-memory access is required.

Sources:
- https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.08472
- https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-kroehl-agentic-trust-aae-02
